title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from neighbouring pages and from the orders of the groups. 𝔊 is (the profinite completion of) a group containing SL2(Z)-type data. Its elliptic stabilizers are L_ρ ≅ Z/6 (the order-3 point ρ, times ±1) and L_σ ≅ Z/4 (the point i). π̂ = π̂_0 × μ with μ = {±1}. This fits π̂ = Γ(2)^ and π̂_0 = a free profinite group of rank 2, i.e. π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}), with 𝔊/π̂ ≅ S_3 = SL2(Z/2). 𝔐 is an ambient group of (outer) automorphisms or normalizers in which the 'équation des lacets' (GT-type relations) is studied. S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} is a group of triples (u,a,b) with u ∈ Z_{ρ,σ} (a centralizer-type group), a ∈ N*_ρ, b ∈ N*_σ (normalizers of the elliptic stabilizers). It is an extension of Z^!_{ρ,σ} = M^![σ] by L_ρ × L_σ.

The proposition (stated on the previous sheet) singles out the subset S_0^πΓ^! of triples with u ≡ b mod π̂_0 and u ≡ ε_3(σ)a mod π̂. This page proves it.
(a) It is a subgroup. As in the computations of pp. 597'–598, closure of the product (u',c',b')(u,c,b) reduces to the commutator condition (56) [σ̇, u̇'] = ε̇'_3, now read in 𝔐/π̂ rather than 𝔐/π̂_0. Equivalently, (56 bis) [u̇', σ̇] = u̇'(σ̇)σ̇^{-1} = ε̇'_2. In 𝔊/π̂_0 the elements ε̇'_2 and ε̇'_3 both lie in the central subgroup π̂/π̂_0 ≅ μ. Hence they become trivial in 𝔊/π̂, and the condition holds automatically.
(b) The projection to Z^!_{ρ,σ} is surjective, because S_0^πΓ^! contains the set-theoretic lift A(Z^!_{ρ,σ}) constructed in the proposition of p. 597.
(c) The kernel consists of the (1,a,b) with a ∈ N*_ρ ∩ π̂ and b ∈ N*_σ ∩ π̂_0. Using N*_ρ ∩ 𝔊 = L_ρ, N*_σ ∩ 𝔊 = L_σ, and (57) L_ρ∩π̂ = L_σ∩π̂ = μ, L_ρ∩π̂_0 = L_σ∩π̂_0 = {1}, the kernel is {(1,ε,1) : ε ∈ μ} ≅ Z/2.

Purpose: this isolates, inside the extension of Z^! by Z/2 × Z/3 × Z/4, the residual Z/2-extension that encodes the sign ambiguity in lifting α from π̂/±1 to π̂ (next page). That ambiguity is later removed by a normalisation of the type α ∈ F̂_{1,2}·π̂_3.
errors: Gap: the claim that ε̇'_2 and ε̇'_3 land in the centre π̂/π̂_0 is asserted, not re-proved here; it relies on earlier pages.
The kernel computation also implicitly uses a ≡ ε_3(σ)^{-1} mod π̂ with ε_3 trivial on the kernel. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Subgroup of triples (u,a,b) cut out by congruences mod π̂_0 and mod π̂ = π̂_0×{±1}, with closure reduced to a commutator condition that becomes trivial modulo the central ±1.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting automorphisms of the profinite modular group / Γ(2)^ along a central ±1 extension; normalizer computations in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Lochak–Schneps for GT and SL2(Z)^ actions
ideas.where_published: Themes appear in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Kernel of the projection identified as μ = {±1}, using that elliptic stabilizers meet Γ(2)^ only in ±1 and the free part trivially.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion in profinite completions of SL2(Z) and of congruence subgroups

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification step (subgroup property, surjectivity, kernel ≅ ±1) inside Grothendieck's long computation on the 'équation des lacets'. It is technically correct and has no apparent novelty beyond its place in his unpublished development.
transcription_corrections: The archive page number at the bottom left is 591; the transcription header and the neighbouring pages carry other numbers (Grothendieck's own pagination such as 599/500).

The line in the transcription read as 'elles [?] rangent [?] ε̇'_2 et ε̇'_3 [?] toutes deux [?] un sous-groupe central' most likely reads 'ε̇'_2 et ε̇'_3 appartiennent toutes deux au sous-groupe central π/π_0'.
In 'N*_ρ ∩ 𝔊 = L_ρ' a struck-out 'Z_ρ' precedes L_ρ.
The struck line before (57) is a crossed-out first attempt 'L_ρ ∩ π_0 = ...'.
The symbol π in 'π/π_0' and 'a ∈ N*_ρ ∩ π' should carry a hat (π̂), consistent with (57).
The line read in the transcription as 'soit ε̇'_3 = ε̇'_2[?]' looks like 'soit ε̇'_3 = ε̇'_1' or 'ε̇'_2'; the index is uncertain.
